newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB: Russia 1997 winter rye output seen down.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB: Russia 1997 winter rye output seen down.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIA: WINTER RYE OUTPUT FORECAST AT 4.8 MLN T, DOWN 18 PCT
Russia's winter rye output in 1997 is expected to total 4.8 million tonnes, a downward revision of 100,000 tonnes from the previous estimate and around 18 percent down on year-ago levels.
This would be the lowest winter rye harvest, after 1995, since the early 1970s.
The forecast range for the winter rye crop this year is 4.3 to 5.1 million tonnes.
For grains as a whole, winterkill losses are estimated at 0.85 million hectares this season, compared with 1.2 million hectares last year.
This would represent about seven percent of the total area sown to winter grains, compared with eight percent in 1995/96 and an average of around 12 percent in 1991/92-1995/96.
In the North Caucasus and Central Chernozem (Black Earth) regions, Russia's wheat belt, winterkill losses are abnormally low and weather conditions for crop development remain good and satisfactory.

At the same time, winterkill losses in the Urals are quite high for the second year in a row. The region, which is Russia's second largest rye producing area, is likely to have a reduced rye harvest this year.
SovEcon's forecast for Russia's total winter wheat output in 1997 remains unchanged in a range of 16-17.5 million tonnes, compared with the 1996 total of 17.1 million tonnes.
